chat.json.notes: Derived from openai/chat.json with the variation many compatible servers show: usage without prompt_tokens_details, so the cache split is unknown.

chat.final-usage.sse.notes: Usage on the chunk that carries finish_reason (no separate usage-only chunk), then data: [DONE]; chunks omit the usage key entirely rather than sending null.

chat.no-done.sse.notes: OpenAI-style final usage chunk but the server closes without data: [DONE]: the usage is observed, but Chat Completions finality requires [DONE], so the exchange is not settled.

deepseek-chat.json.notes: DOCUMENTED, not recorded live: the response example of https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion (read 2026-11-14), model and content replaced. prompt_tokens equals prompt_cache_hit_tokens + prompt_cache_miss_tokens, and prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens is 'Same as prompt_cache_hit_tokens'. Replayed under usage_semantics deepseek, which records cache_write_tokens 0 because input is hit + miss only.

deepseek-chat-cache-hit.json.notes: DERIVED from deepseek-chat.json with a context-cache hit: 1024 hit + 176 miss = 1200 prompt tokens, cached_tokens equal to the hit count as the documentation states. Not recorded live.

deepseek-chat-cache-hit.sse.notes: DERIVED from the documented stream example: usage is null on every chunk except the last content chunk, which carries finish_reason and the whole request's usage (no separate usage-only chunk), then data: [DONE]. Counts as deepseek-chat-cache-hit.json. Not recorded live.

deepseek-chat-inconsistent.json.notes: DERIVED, deliberately inconsistent: hit 1024 + miss 170 is not prompt_tokens 1200. Under usage_semantics deepseek the cache split is unknown (cache read and cache write both null), input and output stay as reported. Not recorded live.

chat.nousage.sse.notes: Server ignores stream_options.include_usage: no usage at all.
